title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Bloomberg Europe
items.content_text: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone, and Telefónica are in early talks to form a consortium to bid for the EU's 2 GHz satellite spectrum. The initiative aims to secure a European-controlled operator status for the reserved band, effectively creating a strategic counterweight to SpaceX's Starlink in the consumer direct-to-device satellite market.

items.title: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of US SEC investigation, sources say
items.content_text: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has launched an investigation into Nvidia's accounting practices. Enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential irregularities, a probe that compounds the company's existing challenges, including the leadership scandal and ongoing investigations into illicit chip shipments to China via regional partners.

items.title: Nvidia stock plunges 12%, rides longest weekly losing streak since 2008 financial crisis
items.content_text: Nvidia is facing severe capital market volatility following the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang due to conduct violations, compounded by an SEC inquiry into its accounting practices. Despite interim CEO Colette Kress maintaining optimistic fiscal projections, investors are increasingly concerned about the company's long-term AI leadership and competitive erosion from AMD and Google.

items.title: KKR in Talks to Buy EdgeCore at Valuation of at Least $8 Billion
items.content_text: Private equity firm KKR is in advanced negotiations to acquire data center operator EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure from Partners Group, with a valuation between $8 billion and $10 billion. The acquisition, executed through KKR's Helix platform, aims to consolidate EdgeCore's 2.27+ gigawatts of capacity across key U.S. markets to meet the insatiable demand for AI infrastructure.

items.title: Take-Two says GTA VI generated $3.79B in day-one sales, surpassing the $2.9B lifetime box-office gross of the highest-grossing film Avengers: Endgame (Jennifer Maas/Variety)
items.content_text: Take-Two Interactive’s 'Grand Theft Auto VI', developed by Rockstar Games, generated $3.79 billion in sales on its launch day, surpassing the lifetime global box-office gross of 'Avengers: Endgame' and setting a new record for the entertainment industry. The title, released on PS5 and Xbox, priced at $80-$100, achieved a Metacritic score of 99, cementing its dominant position in interactive entertainment.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s ‘Lying’ Alarmed Nvidia Board Ahead of His Resignation
items.content_text: Nvidia's board of directors ousted CEO Jensen Huang after an investigation confirmed he misled the board for a year regarding his relationship with an employee at Singapore-based Megaspeed and potential national security implications. While external reports focused on foreign intelligence ties, Board Chair Harvey Jones cited a fundamental lack of integrity and violation of corporate governance policies as the primary drivers for the termination.

items.title: Signal blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and Android to stop AI agents from reading private chats
items.content_text: Signal has implemented screenshot blocking on iOS 27 and specific Android versions to counter OS-level AI agents like Siri, Gemini, and Meta's Muse, which can scrape screen contents. Signal warns that these AI agents, often leveraging system-level permissions or accessibility tools, undermine end-to-end encryption by extracting decrypted messages directly from the display interface.

items.title: Canada Retail Sales Tracking Largest Decline Since Feb. 2025
items.content_text: Statistics Canada reports an estimated 1.5% decline in retail sales for October, marking the sharpest drop since February 2025. CIBC senior economist Andrew Grantham noted that the decline reflects broader volume contraction and stagnant labor market growth, signaling weakening economic momentum heading into the final quarter of 2026.

items.title: Google's Gemini can now run Mac apps and finish desktop chores in the background while you keep working
items.content_text: Google has integrated the 'Computer Use' feature into its Gemini Mac app, allowing the AI to simulate mouse clicks, keyboard inputs, and menu navigation within isolated background windows. This enables the autonomous execution of multi-step tasks across local files and web applications while allowing users to maintain foreground workflow continuity.

items.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US
items.content_text: U.S. President Donald Trump has proposed a 'tremendous tax' on American companies that construct AI data centers outside the country. This policy initiative is framed as a matter of national security, aiming to prevent the offshore migration of critical computing infrastructure and ensure the sovereignty of the domestic AI supply chain.

items.title: YouTube Finalizing Multibillion-Dollar Settlement With Schools Over Social Media Addiction Claims
items.content_text: YouTube, a subsidiary of Alphabet, is finalizing an agreement-in-principle with various U.S. school districts to settle litigation regarding the addictive nature of its platform features. The proposed settlement is valued at approximately $3 billion, with final execution expected to take several months.

items.title: Trump says he would block US companies from building data centers overseas or impose a "tremendous tax" on them if they do (Julianna Bragg/Axios)
items.content_text: Former President Donald Trump proposed a policy aimed at anchoring AI infrastructure within the U.S., threatening to block American companies from constructing data centers abroad or imposing heavy taxes if they do so. This policy stance follows heightened voter concern over the environmental and financial impacts of domestic data center expansion, though the legal mechanism for implementing such taxes remains unclear given Congressional oversight.

items.title: Spying Suspect’s Chip Network Has Ties to Chinese Military Suppliers
items.content_text: Intelligence firm Strider Technologies identified that Alice Huang and her associates built a complex network utilizing $3.6 billion in Chinese government funding for data centers equipped with Nvidia AI chips. The investigation reveals that these entities maintain deep ties to Chinese military contractors and the Ministry of State Security, posing significant compliance risks regarding the diversion of restricted hardware into military research.

items.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.content_text: Nonprofit evaluation group METR has updated its time-horizon plot for AI capabilities, indicating that models show exponential growth in verifiable tasks like coding and mathematics, but lag in judgment-based tasks that lack automated verification. The report highlights the technological bottleneck in applying reinforcement learning to complex, open-ended research decisions, a capability critical for future autonomous R&D.

items.title: Top Republican Senator Says Lutnick Ignored His China Chip Warnings
items.content_text: Senator Tom Cotton, Chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of repeatedly ignoring warnings regarding the smuggling of AI chips to China. This criticism, following the Nvidia scandal, highlights growing congressional dissatisfaction with the Department of Commerce's regulatory oversight and enforcement efficacy.

items.title: Trump, Xi agreed humans must stay in charge of AI military decisions, Bessent says
items.content_text: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed during their meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen that humans must maintain control over military decisions involving artificial intelligence, prohibiting autonomous 'superintelligence' (SI) in major military actions, as confirmed by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The leaders also engaged in robust discussions regarding nuclear non-proliferation, trade policy, and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, culminating in a joint declaration emphasizing that nuclear war must never be fought.

items.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
items.content_text: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics’s most notoriously difficult problems, with the help of Claude, cracking a puzzle that has eluded some of the world’s best mathematicians for decades. If verified, it would mark yet another seismic achievement for AI in mathematics and add to the upheaval already unleashed by OpenAI’s previous, often inelegant forays into the field. Alpöge’s solution has yet to be verified independently. Anthro

items.title: Linq, which offers texting and calling infrastructure for AI agents, raised a $90M Series B led by a16z, following a $20M Series A in February (Harper Harwell/Birmingham Business Journal)
items.content_text: Linq, a provider of specialized communication infrastructure for AI agents, has secured $90 million in Series B funding led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). This financing follows a $20 million Series A round in February, underscoring rapid capital deployment into the foundational connectivity layer of the AI agent ecosystem.

items.title: Bloomberg analysis of 10 million job postings shows AI-exposed roles in China fell 10 percentage points faster than others
items.content_text: of nearly 10 million job postings reveals that AI is significantly disrupting China's labor market, disproportionately affecting entry-level and creative roles. Vulnerable positions have seen a demand decline 10 percentage points sharper than non-impacted roles, with research from ShanghaiTech University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences confirming structural shifts including role consolidation and quiet staff reductions at major internet firms.

items.title: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he used Claude to prove the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis and posts the proof in the Lean programming language (Joseph Howlett/Scientific American)
items.content_text: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician and employee at artificial intelligence company Anthropic, claimed on Friday to have proven the most famous problem in all of mathematics using an LLM. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote in a statement posted on his website. items.title: Anthropic Share Slump Nearly Erases IPO Pop As AI Trade Unravels
items.content_text: Anthropic PBC shares erased much of their first-day jump on Friday, testing investors' faith after the AI lab delivered the biggest initial public offering in history.

items.title: Apple joins the race for AI agents that control your device while raising new barriers for competitors
items.content_text: After Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google launched their own AI agents, Apple is now building one too - while making it harder for rivals to access its devices. According to a job listing, Apple is hiring a senior engineer to lead the project as a rival to Muse, Dots, Duet, and Grok Bots. Privacy is expected to be central to the new agent, with permission models and sandboxing (protected test environments). According to Bloomberg, the agent could arrive as early as late next year, though it rem

items.title: Nvidia bets at least $500 million on Inception's diffusion models to strengthen its open-source Nemotron lineup
items.content_text: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire AI startup Inception for at least $500 million, including full-time integration of founders Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, and Volodymyr Kuleshov. Inception specializes in diffusion-based language models, such as Mercury 3, which refine responses globally rather than token-by-token. This acquisition is designed to enhance Nvidia's Nemotron open-source lineup and accelerate its physical simulation capabilities for robotics.

items.title: The week everything fell apart
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is embroiled in a growing scandal involving the alleged illegal smuggling of chips to China, fueling speculation regarding his potential exit. The core controversy centers on Nvidia’s compliance failures and internal control deficiencies amid increasingly stringent US export restrictions.

items.title: Anthropic raises $93.5 billion total as underwriters scoop up ‘greenshoe’ overallotment
items.content_text: AI firm Anthropic completed its historic IPO on Nasdaq, raising a total of $93.5 billion after underwriters exercised the greenshoe option for an additional $12.2 billion. Simultaneously, the company closed a $26 billion private placement involving major tech entities like AMD, Google, Microsoft, and Nvidia, bringing total gross proceeds to $119.5 billion.

items.title: Google's latest homepage update pushes its search engine further toward an AI answer engine
items.content_text: Google is rolling out a collapsible sidebar globally on its Desktop Search homepage, making AI search even easier to access. Announced on X by Google Search VP Robby Stein, the feature lets users easily find and reopen recent AI searches. Sitting on the left side of the AI Mode interface, it lets users start new threads, search existing ones, create notebooks, and open recent queries and settings. Stein said people are increasingly asking Google Search questions that a single query can't answer

items.title: Uber tests rides for kids as young as 10, with extra pay for drivers
items.content_text: Uber has launched the 'Uber Kids' pilot program in Austin, Nashville, and Madison, lowering the minimum ride-hailing age to 10. The service mandates parental onboarding, real-time video monitoring, PIN verification, and GPS-based off-course detection, while offering participating high-rated drivers a $7 premium per trip.

items.title: Threats, Insults, Settlements: How Jensen Huang Made Humiliation Routine
items.content_text: Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly utilized aggressive management tactics, allegedly stating that as employees achieve financial independence due to the company's soaring market cap, humiliation becomes the primary tool to ensure continued high-intensity output. This governance philosophy has triggered internal concerns regarding organizational cohesion and long-term talent retention.

items.title: Threats, Insults, Settlements: How Jensen Huang Made Humiliation Routine
items.content_text: As Nvidia became wealthier and wealthier in recent years, Jensen Huang grew increasingly frustrated with his staff. He told groups of subordinates that they had become so rich that he couldn’t motivate them simply with money, according to three people who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss confidential conversations.
